overview: This House resolution approves the House's final changes to H.R. 6644, a large housing bill that the Senate had amended, replacing the Senate's version with a new text called the "21st Century ROAD to Housing Act" and sending it back to the Senate. That text has dozens of parts aimed at expanding the housing supply and access to homeownership, including grants for home repairs for lower-income owners, letting factory-built homes be built without a permanent steel chassis, a possible pilot program to make small mortgages easier to get through the Federal Housing Administration, reforms to the HOME affordable housing program and rural housing programs, and easier rules for community banks. It would generally bar large institutional investors, defined as those controlling at least 350 single-family homes, from buying more single-family homes, with exceptions such as homes built to rent or renovated and resold, backed by fines of up to $1 million per violation or three times the purchase price. It would also bar the Federal Reserve from issuing a central bank digital currency (a digital dollar issued directly by the Fed) through 2030. The House agreed to the resolution on May 20, 2026, which sent the revised bill back to the Senate.
for: Supporters say the package tackles the housing shortage from many angles at once, cutting red tape for building, helping first-time and lower-income buyers, and keeping large investors from outbidding families for starter homes.
against: Critics say the package bundles many unrelated policies, such as banking rules and a ban on a Federal Reserve digital currency, into one housing bill, and that limits on investor purchases could reduce rental housing and investment in homes.
